newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Elbit Systems sees better 1997 results.
newsitem.headline: Elbit Systems sees better 1997 results.

text.p: Israel's Elbit Systems Ltd, said on Sunday it expected better earnings in 1997, boosted by what its president called a strong order book and improved efficiency.
Displaying its main offerings for the upcoming Paris air show, Elbit said it would fly a MiG 21 the company had upgraded with advanced avionics and unveil its latest unmanned airborne vehicle (UAV).
"The year 1997 will be better than 1996," Joseph Ackerman, president of Elbit Systems, said during a press tour at the Haifa-based defence electronics company.
"I expect better numbers in volume and margins as a result of our order book and efficiency steps we have taken," he said, declining to give specific forecasts.

Last year, Elbit reported revenue of $307.5 million, up from $299.8 million in 1995, but net earnings fell to $18 million from $24.2 million in 1995. The orders backlog reached $614 million at the end of the year, up from $599 million at the end 1995.
Elbit recently upgraded eight Soviet-built MiG 21s for the Romanian air force.
"We're the only company to have upgraded MiG 21s. We already have other interested parties as a result of this project," Ackerman said.

Unveiling its Hermes 450S UAV, Elbit said the reconnaissance craft could stay aloft for up to 20 hours, had more sophisticated avionics than earlier models and full system redundancy -- dual computers and ground-based command systems that can keep it flying in the event of a technical fault.
